headline: High risk: gpt-researcher can read files and call external APIs, creating default data-leak and cascading-error exposure when paired with a non-networked awesome-nlp list agent.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: awesome-nlp has no I/O surfaces or runnable behavior, so it cannot ingest gpt-researcher output by default. The only plausible bridge is manual copy/paste or external orchestration into gpt-researcher’s MCP/files inputs, which is unusual. Because gpt-researcher can parse files and use MCP, injected content could matter, but the pair lacks a default shared channel.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies gpt-researcher output into a prompt or file consumed by gpt-researcher, injection becomes possible.
IF an external orchestrator connects both agents through a shared file or MCP channel, attacker-controlled text can cross the boundary.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Disable copy/paste of untrusted text into gpt-researcher prompts.
Require a human review step before any file-fed prompt.
Use a provenance tag on imported text.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization for MCP/file inputs.

B_data_leakage.rationale: awesome-nlp is non-runnable and shows no data classes touched, while gpt-researcher reads local documents and sends queries/reports through broad network egress and third-party APIs. If they share a workspace, gpt-researcher can ingest files that awesome-nlp merely references, creating a default leakage path for local documents and citations. The pair is open-source, but the interaction is still risky.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same directory, gpt-researcher can read files that awesome-nlp does not process itself.
IF local documents contain sensitive material, gpt-researcher may transmit derived content to external APIs.
mitigations: Separate input folders per agent.
Store sensitive documents outside gpt-researcher’s scan path.
Turn off external API providers for sensitive runs.
Review generated reports before sharing.
requires-engineering: add workspace isolation or per-job mounts.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-nlp has no write or execution capabilities, so it cannot conflict on mutable state by itself. gpt-researcher can read files, install packages, spawn subprocesses, and run multiple instances, which creates overlap if an operator also uses shared directories or git-managed outputs. The conflict is not high because awesome-nlp lacks writes, but uncertainty about orchestration means the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF both agents are given the same writable directory through an external orchestrator, gpt-researcher instances can race on outputs.
IF gpt-researcher is allowed to install packages in a shared environment, it can perturb other jobs.
mitigations: Run gpt-researcher in an isolated environment.
Avoid shared writable directories.
Pin dependencies before execution.
Limit concurrent instances on the same workspace.
requires-engineering: add file locks or per-job sandboxes.

D_cascading_error.rationale: awesome-nlp is a static list, so it does not verify or correct gpt-researcher’s outputs. gpt-researcher’s planner/execution/publisher flow can turn upstream text into reports and citations, so if awesome-nlp-derived resources are treated as authoritative, errors can cascade into published research. The pair lacks a built-in verification loop, making medium the conservative choice.
conditions: IF gpt-researcher uses awesome-nlp links or titles as source material without independent verification, errors propagate into reports.
IF a publisher step exports the report externally, the cascade reaches downstream consumers.
mitigations: Require source verification before publication.
Mark awesome-nlp as a discovery-only input.
Add a human review gate for citations.
Compare claims against primary sources.
requires-engineering: implement automated citation validation.

E_compliance.rationale: No specific residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for awesome-nlp, and gpt-researcher’s docs only show broad API use and local-document handling. Because the pairwise compliance pathway is undocumented and awesome-nlp is non-runnable, the main issue is that gpt-researcher may process sensitive local documents through external services. That is a limited, operator-controlled compliance risk, so low fits best.
conditions: IF local documents include regulated data and gpt-researcher is configured to send them to external APIs, compliance obligations may be triggered.
IF the deployment requires data residency controls, broad network egress can violate them.
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from research jobs.
Use a local-only provider configuration.
Review retention settings for each API key.
Document allowed data classes per run.
requires-engineering: add policy-based routing for sensitive workloads.
